articles.title: JP Morgan Says AI Is Deflating India's IT Giants. It Picked Two Winners.
articles.excerpt: The brokerage expects only 3-4% growth for Indian IT services as AI compresses delivery timelines. TCS and Infosys are favoured; HCLTech and Wipro are not.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of the glass pyramid at the Infosys campus in Mysore, India
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of NRIs work at Indian IT firms or hold their stocks — this downgrade signals structural change in the industry that built the diaspora's professional class.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI's First Hardware Is a Macro Pad for Coders. It Launches July 15.
articles.excerpt: The Codex Micro, built with keyboard maker Work Louder, gives developers physical buttons for AI-assisted coding shortcuts. It is not the Jony Ive device.
articles.image_caption: A mechanical keyboard and macro pad with LED lighting on an ergonomic desk setup
articles.nri_angle: India has the world's second-largest developer community and OpenAI just hired ex-Uber India chief Prabhjeet Singh as its India MD — this hardware play signals growing investment in the developer ecosystem Indian engineers dominate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Tech Workers Are Self-Sponsoring Their Green Cards. EB-1A Filings Have Jumped 50%.
articles.excerpt: With H-1B costs soaring and layoffs triggering 60-day exit clocks, senior Indian engineers are bypassing employer-sponsored immigration entirely. The EB-1A 'extraordinary ability' visa is their escape hatch.
articles.image_caption: H-1B visa application documents at the US Citizenship and Immigration Services
articles.nri_angle: EB-1A self-petitions directly affect tens of thousands of Indian H-1B professionals in the US — this is the immigration strategy shift of a generation for the tech diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Tells India Its Antitrust Case Was 'Copy-Pasted.' The Fine Could Hit $38 Billion.
articles.excerpt: In its sharpest legal filing yet, Apple accuses the CCI of recycling rivals' complaints rather than conducting independent analysis — but India's regulators have heard that argument before, from Google.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of Apple Park in Cupertino, California — headquarters of a company now facing up to $38 billion in antitrust exposure in India
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin iOS developers and fintech founders on both sides of the Pacific could see fundamental changes to how the App Store operates in India, while PhonePe — widely used by NRIs for cross-border payments — is among the complainants.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Building 20 AI Models to Rival ChatGPT. Its Strategy Is to Skip the Arms Race.
articles.excerpt: As the US restricts its most powerful AI systems, India is funding homegrown open-source models that deliver 60-80% of frontier capability — and betting that's enough for most of the world.
articles.image_caption: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology is driving the country's sovereign AI push, including 20 indigenous large language models
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin AI researchers at Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic now have open-source Indian models to build on, while NRI investors get exposure to a government-backed AI ecosystem producing tangible outputs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Companies Spending the Most on AI Are Hiring the Fastest. The Full Story Is More Complicated.
articles.excerpt: A new study of 22,000 companies finds heavy AI adopters grew headcount 10%. But 185,000 tech workers lost jobs this year, and Indians on H-1B are the most exposed population of all.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of artificial intelligence and machine learning — the technology reshaping both hiring and layoff patterns across Silicon Valley
articles.nri_angle: Indians hold the largest share of H-1B visas and are disproportionately affected by AI-driven layoffs, while senior Indian engineers are increasingly pursuing EB-1A green cards to decouple their immigration status from volatile employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI's New India Chief Is an IIT-IIM Alum Who Ran Uber for a Decade
articles.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh, who expanded Uber across India and South Asia for 11 years, will lead OpenAI's second-largest market. He starts in September.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI headquarters at the Pioneer Building in San Francisco. Credit: Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: An IIT Kharagpur and IIM Ahmedabad alumnus now leads OpenAI's India strategy — a signal that the AI labs are drawing from the same elite Indian talent pipeline as FAANG, with product decisions increasingly shaped by India's 100 million ChatGPT users.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Agnikul Just Signed a Deal to Launch Radar Satellites. The Partner Is Finnish.
articles.excerpt: Agnikul Cosmos and Finland's ICEYE will build sovereign SAR satellite capabilities in India, announced at the Bharat Innovates summit with Modi and Macron present.
articles.image_caption: ISRO LVM3 rocket on its launch pad in India. Credit: ISRO/Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: India's private space sector is becoming a real investment and career proposition for NRIs in aerospace — Agnikul's $500M valuation and sovereign SAR satellite deal represent both return-to-India pathways and cross-border business opportunities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Gave Its AI Agent a Desktop. It Costs $100 a Month and It Wants Your Files.
articles.excerpt: Gemini Spark launched on macOS with third-party integrations, real-time tracking, and an Indian-origin DeepMind VP leading the engineering. The desktop agent war is on.
articles.image_caption: Google CEO Sundar Pichai at a public event in 2023
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin VP of Engineering at Google DeepMind co-leads the Gemini Spark launch. For millions of Indian tech professionals using Google Workspace, the choice of desktop AI agent is becoming as consequential as the choice of operating system a decade ago.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SK Hynix Is Coming to Nasdaq on July 10. Mehrotra's Micron Just Lost Its American Monopoly.
articles.excerpt: The South Korean chipmaker that dominates high-bandwidth memory plans a $29 billion ADR listing — arriving on the same exchange as Micron, and directly in the sightlines of every NRI portfolio that rode the AI memory trade.
articles.image_caption: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra at a 2025 event
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who bet on Micron for its Indian CEO and Gujarat fab now face a second memory stock on Nasdaq that could split passive index flows and compress Micron's valuation premium.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Is Lobbying Washington to Buy Chips from a Blacklisted Chinese Company. The Price Tag Explains Why.
articles.excerpt: Memory costs are soaring so fast that Apple raised Mac and iPad prices by up to 25 per cent — and is now asking the Trump administration for clearance to source DRAM from CXMT, a Chinese chipmaker on the Pentagon's military-linked list.
articles.image_caption: Apple CEO Tim Cook — the company is lobbying Washington to allow purchases from blacklisted Chinese chipmaker YMTC (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The AI memory crunch affects every NRI in tech — from Micron's Gujarat fab and Indian chip ambitions to the iPhone 18 pricing that hits every consumer's wallet.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World's Central Bankers Just Held a Meeting. Every Conversation Was About AI.
articles.excerpt: At the ECB's annual Sintra forum, the architects of global monetary policy compared the AI investment boom to the dotcom crash and the railway mania of the 1840s. For NRI tech workers and investors, the warning is personal.
articles.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh at the ECB Sintra forum, where he called the AI revolution the biggest economic event of our lifetime
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B workers make up 70 per cent of US tech visa holders and NRI portfolios are heavily concentrated in AI stocks — both are directly exposed if central bankers are right about an AI-driven correction.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Noida Kid's BASIC Program Led to an $8.3 Billion AI Company. Together AI Just Raised $800 Million.
articles.excerpt: Vipul Ved Prakash's open-source cloud platform, backed by Aramco, Nvidia and Salesforce, is becoming the infrastructure layer the AI industry didn't know it needed.
articles.image_caption: Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO of Together AI
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin founder from Noida builds $8.3B AI infrastructure company; platform enables affordable AI for Indian startups like Sarvam AI and Krutrim; major hiring pipeline from Indian engineering talent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Is Building a Cloud Business. The Neoclouds It Hired Are Already Bleeding.
articles.excerpt: Zuckerberg's company plans to sell excess AI computing capacity, sending CoreWeave and Nebius stocks into freefall and reshaping the cloud landscape Indian IT firms depend on.
articles.image_caption: Meta headquarters in Menlo Park, California — the company is building a cloud computing business to rent out AI infrastructure (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian engineers work at Meta and neocloud firms facing strategic upheaval; Indian IT services giants (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) may need to build expertise around a fourth hyperscaler; cheaper AI compute benefits Indian startups.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Government Froze Anthropic's Best AI for 17 Days. Then It Unfroze It. The Damage Was Already Done.
articles.excerpt: Export controls on Claude Fable 5 locked out foreign-national employees — including Indian engineers — and threw a trillion-dollar IPO into doubt. The ban is lifted. The precedent is not.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, at TechCrunch Disrupt
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI researchers on H-1B visas were locked out of their own models at Anthropic; episode exposes a new regulatory risk for Indian professionals at frontier AI labs; India's own AI governance framework must account for this kind of precedent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Shipped Its First Semiconductor Chips. They Went to Malaysia.
articles.excerpt: CG Semi's Gujarat plant dispatched its first commercial consignment of packaged microcontrollers for Renesas — a quiet milestone in India's $20 billion chip ambition.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of a semiconductor fabrication plant — India has begun shipping its first domestically produced chips (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin semiconductor engineers across Silicon Valley and Austin now have a domestic chip ecosystem beginning to take shape — one that could pull NRI talent and investment back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel's Former Chief Architect Raised $60 Million to Break Nvidia's Lock on AI. His Weapon Is a Blueprint.
articles.excerpt: Raja Koduri's startup Oxmiq wants to be the Arm of artificial intelligence — licensing unified chip IP so anyone can build competitive AI hardware without spending $500 million.
articles.image_caption: Jim Keller, former Intel chief architect and CEO of Tenstorrent (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Koduri's IIT-to-Intel-to-founder arc represents the Indian semiconductor diaspora at its most ambitious — and a more open AI chip ecosystem would expand opportunities for thousands of Indian-origin chip designers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ford's AI Replaced Its Best Engineers. Then Ford Had to Hire Them All Back.
articles.excerpt: Indian-American COO Kumar Galhotra admits the automaker over-relied on automation — and the 350 veteran engineers it rehired just delivered Ford's best quality ranking in 16 years.
articles.image_caption: Ford Motor Company headquarters in Dearborn, Michigan (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Ford COO Kumar Galhotra — an IIT graduate and one of Detroit's most senior Indian-origin executives — publicly admitted AI cannot replace domain expertise, a reassuring data point for 300,000 Indian engineers in the US on H-1B visas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oracle's AI Purge Hit India Hardest. 12,000 Workers Got an Email at 6 AM.
articles.excerpt: The world's largest enterprise software company cut 21,000 jobs in twelve months. Roughly half were in India — its biggest hub outside the United States.
articles.image_caption: Oracle headquarters campus in Redwood City, California
articles.nri_angle: 12,000-15,000 Indian workers lost jobs at Oracle's largest international hub; H-1B holders in the US face the 60-day clock in an industry that has shed 185,000 jobs this year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Joins the Nasdaq-100 on July 7. Your 401(k) Is About to Own a Rocket Company.
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk's $2 trillion space and AI company enters the most popular growth index after just 15 trading days. If you hold QQQ in your retirement account, you will become a SpaceX investor next week — whether you planned to or not.
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket during launch
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs hold QQQ and Nasdaq-100 index funds in their 401(k) and IRA accounts; SpaceX's forced inclusion changes their portfolio exposure, and Starlink's pending India entry adds a personal stake.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and America Are Quietly Building an AI Pact. The Diaspora Is the Bridge.
articles.excerpt: As Modi visits Washington, India's ambassador met with top US tech and defence leaders while American universities build AI schools across India. The alliance is deeper than the headlines suggest.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Modi with world leaders at the AI Action Summit in Paris, February 2025
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans sit at the intersection of US AI capability and Indian deployment potential — running the companies, staffing the labs, and now shaping the policy frameworks that govern both sides.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Persistent Just Bet €1 Billion on a German Firm It Barely Knows. The Market Thinks It Overpaid.
articles.excerpt: India's fastest-growing mid-tier IT company launched its biggest acquisition ever — and its stock hit a 15-month low while regulators probe a suspicious price surge.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange — Persistent Systems shares fell sharply after the company announced a €1 billion acquisition that investors deemed overpriced (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Persistent employs thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas in the US; the merger reshapes the mid-tier IT career landscape and affects NRI investors holding the stock at a 15-month low.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Tokens Now Cost More Than Some Developers. Companies Are Budgeting Them Like Salaries.
articles.excerpt: Goldman predicts a 24-fold surge in enterprise AI token consumption. Companies are capping usage, and a price war between OpenAI and Anthropic is reshaping how every tech team spends.
articles.image_caption: Inside a data center — enterprises are now budgeting AI inference tokens as a line item alongside developer salaries (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT services companies deploy AI models for global clients and face margin pressure as token costs spike; Indian engineers on H-1B visas at tech companies will be directly affected by AI cost restructuring.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Told Its Banks to Treat Every AI Model Like a Risk Model. The Rules Are Sweeping.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's draft guidelines mandate board-approved AI policies, independent model validation, and human oversight — reshaping how HDFC, ICICI, and every fintech in the country deploys artificial intelligence.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters building in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors in Indian bank stocks face rising compliance costs; Indian-origin fintech founders building products on Indian banking rails must now comply with AI model governance mandates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Qualcomm Just Spent $4 Billion to Break Nvidia's Software Lock. It May Spend $10 Billion More.
articles.excerpt: The Modular acquisition gives Qualcomm a CUDA rival. A Tenstorrent deal would give it an AI chip army. Meta and Microsoft are already signing up.
articles.image_caption: Qualcomm headquarters in San Diego, California
articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm is one of the largest H-1B employers of Indian engineers. Its AI pivot revalues mobile-computing skills overnight — and its Hyderabad, Bangalore, and Chennai R&D centres are central to the effort.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CRED's Kunal Shah Is Now Running WhatsApp. Meta Paid $900 Million for That Handshake.
articles.excerpt: The Indian founder who made credit card bills aspirational has been hired to monetise the world's largest messaging app. He'll do it from Bengaluru.
articles.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED and new global CEO of WhatsApp
articles.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the lifeline between NRIs and family in India. An Indian founder now runs the app that 500 million Indians use daily — and he's been hired to make it a commerce platform.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nadella's Microsoft Is About to Cut 5,700 Jobs. Xbox May Never Recover.
articles.excerpt: A 2.5% workforce reduction across sales, consulting, and gaming is expected as early as next week — with the Xbox division bracing for what insiders call the largest single layoff event in gaming history.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft is one of the largest H-1B employers in the US. Thousands of Indian engineers in Redmond, Hyderabad, and Bangalore face an uncertain July as the company restructures around AI — and the 60-day visa clock starts ticking for anyone caught in the cuts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard, and Google Just Launched a Stablecoin. It Has 140 Partners and Zero Fees.
articles.excerpt: Open USD, backed by a consortium that includes BlackRock, Stripe, and Coinbase, is designed to become the default digital dollar for global payments — and it could reshape how NRIs send money home.
articles.image_caption: Visa and Mastercard — the payments giants have partnered with Google to launch a stablecoin with 140 partners and zero transaction fees (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans send over $100 billion in remittances annually. A zero-fee, consortium-backed stablecoin endorsed by the payment networks they already use could dramatically lower the cost of moving money between the US and India — if RBI regulations allow it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata Communications Has Replaced Its CEO, CFO, and CTO in Five Months. A Data Centre Fire Explains Why.
articles.excerpt: The Indian telecom giant's third C-suite appointment of 2026 brings in an Akamai and AT&T veteran as CTO, as the company races to rebuild credibility after a devastating fire at its New Delhi data centre and accelerate its AI infrastructure push.
articles.image_caption: Vinod Kumar, former CEO and Managing Director of Tata Communications, who was replaced as part of a sweeping leadership overhaul (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Tata Communications runs the backbone infrastructure that connects India's digital economy to the world — and its data centres are where many NRI-facing services actually live. A leadership reset of this scale at a Tata Group company signals both crisis and ambition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pichai's Google Ran Out of GPUs. So It's Paying a Rocket Company $920 Million a Month.
articles.excerpt: Google capped Meta's Gemini access, leased compute from SpaceX, and still can't keep up with demand. The AI infrastructure crisis is no longer hypothetical.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google, at a 2023 event
articles.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's compute crunch directly affects Indian engineers at Google Cloud and Meta, and downstream capacity for Indian IT firms building on Gemini Enterprise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Opened a Factory That Makes Data for Humanoid Robots. Production Workers Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: Apptronik's Robot Park in Austin is training fleets of Apollo 2 humanoids with Google DeepMind's AI. Real deployments start in 2027.
articles.image_caption: The Googleplex, Google headquarters in Mountain View, California — the company has opened a dedicated facility for producing training data for humanoid robots (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI researchers at Google DeepMind are driving the Gemini Robotics models, while Indian logistics workers in the US face the automation wave these robots will bring.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FactSet's Indian-Origin CEO Just Plugged Google's AI Directly Into Wall Street's Terminal.
articles.excerpt: Sanoke Viswanathan, a former JPMorgan executive, is partnering with Google Cloud to build agentic AI for the financial industry. The tools 40,000 Indian-origin finance professionals use daily are about to change.
articles.image_caption: FactSet headquarters — the financial data company's Indian-origin CEO has partnered with Google to bring AI agents directly into Wall Street terminals (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEO Sanoke Viswanathan leads FactSet's AI transformation, directly affecting tens of thousands of Indian finance professionals on Wall Street who use FactSet daily.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Narayen Is Leaving Adobe. Both Candidates to Replace Him Are Also Indian.
articles.excerpt: After 18 years, Adobe's Hyderabad-born CEO is stepping down — and the two frontrunners to succeed him, David Wadhwani and Anil Chakravarthy, are also of Indian origin. The diaspora's grip on American enterprise software is tightening.
articles.image_caption: Shantanu Narayen, Adobe's outgoing CEO, who has led the company for 18 years
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin executives dominate Adobe's C-suite — outgoing CEO Narayen and both leading successors are of Indian descent, extending the diaspora's leadership pipeline in enterprise software alongside Nadella at Microsoft and Pichai at Google.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Is Spending $1 Billion to Embed AI Engineers Inside Your Company. The Talent Pool Is Heavily Indian.
articles.excerpt: AWS's new forward-deployed engineering unit will send pods of AI specialists directly to enterprise clients. With Amazon cutting 30,000 corporate jobs while hiring thousands for this initiative, the shift has implications for Indian tech workers on both sides.
articles.image_caption: The Amazon Spheres at the company's Seattle headquarters — the tech giant is deploying  billion to embed AI engineers inside enterprise clients worldwide (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Amazon's massive Indian workforce — both in the US on H-1B visas and in India — makes the diaspora the largest talent pool for this new high-demand role. The initiative also signals which AI jobs are safe from automation and which are not.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Marvell's Stock Just Jumped 7%. Its Largest Lab Outside California Is in India.
articles.excerpt: As the chip company races to build the optical backbone of AI data centres, its biggest R&D hub in India is designing the connectivity silicon that Nvidia, Amazon, and Microsoft need to keep their GPU clusters running.
articles.image_caption: Marvell Technology, the semiconductor firm whose stock surged 7% on its custom AI chip strategy (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Marvell's largest global R&D hub outside its California HQ is in India, making Indian engineers central to the design of connectivity chips that power the world's AI data centres — a story of diaspora engineering influence at the hardware layer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Just Went Live in Athens. The Payment System That Replaced Cash Now Works in 10 Countries.
articles.excerpt: Greece becomes the latest country to accept India's real-time payment rails, in a Eurobank partnership witnessed by Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal — and NRI travellers are the immediate beneficiaries.
articles.image_caption: A contactless QR code payment being made via smartphone (Pexels)
articles.nri_angle: NRI travellers to Greece, Singapore, France, UAE, and six other countries can now pay with the same UPI apps they use at home — no currency conversion fees, no card surcharges, no cash anxiety.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bajaj Got Ransomware. Tata Got Hacked. Then a Data Centre Burned Down. India Inc Had a Terrible June.
articles.excerpt: Three cybersecurity incidents at major Indian conglomerates in three weeks have exposed the gap between India's manufacturing ambitions and its ability to protect the systems that underpin them.
articles.image_caption: A cybersecurity professional monitoring systems on a computer screen in low light
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors hold billions in Tata and Bajaj stock. NRIs working at Apple, Tesla, and Qualcomm — all Tata Electronics clients — now have to wonder whether their employer's supplier can protect their work product.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Just Touched ₹1,000. TCS Lost ₹2,050. The Worst IT Selloff Since Covid Has a Familiar Villain.
articles.excerpt: Every major Indian IT stock fell 2-3.5% on Tuesday as AI deflation, weak guidance, and a global spending freeze converge. NRI investors who held through the pandemic may be staring at round-trip returns.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT stocks are among the most widely held equities by NRI investors. TCS and Infosys are also among the largest employers of H-1B workers in the US — when their stock craters, hiring freezes follow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Krishna's IBM Just Built a Chip Smaller Than One Nanometre. It Packs 100 Billion Transistors.
articles.excerpt: The 'nanostack' architecture stacks transistors in 3D for the first time, pointing to a decade of continued scaling — and raising questions about where India fits in the atomic-scale chip race.
articles.image_caption: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna at SXSW 2025
articles.nri_angle: IBM's Indian-origin CEO Arvind Krishna leads the company behind the world's most consequential chip breakthrough, while India's own semiconductor ambitions remain focused on packaging and assembly rather than foundational transistor research.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'If Coding Becomes Automated, Why Are We Needed?' Nilekani Has an Answer.
articles.excerpt: The Infosys chairman used his annual general meeting speech to confront AI's existential threat to Indian IT — arguing that the bigger the disruption, the bigger the opportunity for services firms.
articles.image_caption: Infosys co-founder and chairman Nandan Nilekani
articles.nri_angle: Over 300,000 Indian IT professionals in the US on H-1B visas face direct career implications as AI reshapes the services industry that employs them; Infosys's 28% stock decline this year has hit NRI investor portfolios hard.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Signed a 35-Nation Pact to Secure AI's Silicon Supply Chain. Here's What It Actually Means.
articles.excerpt: At the second Pax Silica Summit in Washington, India committed to building trusted chip and critical-mineral pipelines alongside the US, EU, and 32 other countries — a move that could reshape careers and investments for the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor wafer — the silicon foundation of the AI supply chain India is now helping to secure
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American chip engineers at Intel, Qualcomm, and NVIDIA stand to benefit from deeper US-India semiconductor cooperation, while India's 85,000-job chip workforce target creates new return-to-India career paths and investment opportunities for NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Arora's Palo Alto Networks Just Hit a $3 Billion Quarter. Then Its Stock Hit an All-Time High.
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO bought $10 million of his own stock when it crashed on AI fears. It has since more than doubled. Palo Alto's record Q3 shows why cybersecurity is the AI boom's biggest beneficiary.
articles.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, at a technology conference
articles.nri_angle: Arora, an IIT Varanasi alumnus, leads the most valuable cybersecurity company in the world — a sector where Indian engineers are in surging demand. NRI investors tracking Indian-origin CEO-led stocks now have a cybersecurity entry point alongside Nadella's Microsoft and Pichai's Alphabet.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Just Bet $48 Billion on India. Jassy Flew to Delhi to Tell Modi Personally.
articles.excerpt: The largest tech investment commitment to India — ever — includes $21 billion for AI and cloud infrastructure alone. Amazon, Microsoft, and Google have collectively earmarked $80 billion for Indian compute capacity in eight months.
articles.image_caption: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy, who met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to announce the $48 billion investment
articles.nri_angle: AWS's $21 billion cloud expansion creates thousands of new cloud/AI roles for Indian-American engineers, while Amazon stock offers NRI investors direct exposure to India's booming digital economy without the complexity of Indian equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Hired an IIT-IIM Grad to Run India. He Built Uber's Indian Empire First.
articles.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh, who turned Uber from a ride-hailing app into an auto-rickshaw platform, will lead OpenAI's push into its second-largest market.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman; the company has appointed former Uber India president Prabhjeet Singh as its first India Managing Director (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: IIT-IIM alumni pipeline now reaches frontier AI leadership; OpenAI's India expansion means new AI jobs in Mumbai/Bengaluru for returning NRIs and signals pricing/product changes that affect diaspora developers using ChatGPT APIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Taiwan Just Raided Super Micro's Offices Over $2.5 Billion in Missing Nvidia Chips. India Should Be Watching.
articles.excerpt: The chip smuggling probe expands as prosecutors search six homes and three companies. For India's semiconductor ambitions, the lesson is about trust as much as technology.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia AI chips — Taiwanese authorities have raided Supermicro offices over .5 billion in missing Nvidia processors allegedly diverted to restricted markets (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers at chip companies face heightened export compliance scrutiny; India's semiconductor ambitions (Tata, Micron Gujarat) depend on being seen as a trusted manufacturing hub in the US-led chip export control regime.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian IT Is Already Making $12 Billion from AI. The Hard Part Is What Comes Next.
articles.excerpt: Nasscom says a quarter of Indian tech firms have moved AI from pilot to production. But JP Morgan's analysts see revenue compression, not expansion. Both sides have a point.
articles.image_caption: Indian IT firms including TCS, Infosys, and Wipro now generate over 2 billion annually from AI-related services (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Indian IT stocks (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) need to parse the gap between Nasscom's bullish AI revenue data and JP Morgan's bearish guidance cuts; engineers considering return-to-India moves should note the shift toward AI-specialist hiring.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Tata Breach Just Got Worse. iPhone 18 Pro Supplier Maps and Drop-Test Photos Are Now on the Dark Web.
articles.excerpt: A Reuters review of newly leaked files reveals component-to-supplier maps, confidential Apple watermarks, and factory photographs of unreleased iPhones — escalating what was already India's biggest corporate cyber breach.
articles.image_caption: Tata Electronics, which assembles iPhones at its Hosur plant, has suffered a breach exposing supplier schematics for Apple's iPhone 18 Pro (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's 26% share of global iPhone production rests on Tata's credibility as Apple's newest major assembler. NRI engineers at Apple, TSMC, and Qualcomm face professional fallout as supplier relationships are exposed; investors in Tata Group companies confront a trust deficit with no clear resolution timeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JP Morgan Just Told Indian IT to Brace for Year Two of AI Deflation. The Numbers Are Getting Worse.
articles.excerpt: A new research note warns that every major Indian IT company faces Q1 FY27 guidance cuts as AI-led pricing erosion enters its second year — and this time, deal closures are stalling too.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru — JP Morgan warns that Indian IT firms face a second year of AI-driven revenue deflation (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian nationals on H-1B visas work at or are subcontracted through these firms; hiring freezes and reduced onsite deployment directly affect visa renewals and green card pipelines. NRI investors hold significant positions in IT stocks that have collectively shed $26 billion in market value this quarter.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mehrotra's Micron Just Posted a $41.5 Billion Quarter. The Man from Kanpur Has Never Had a Hand This Good.
articles.excerpt: Revenue up 346%, margins at 68%, and $22 billion in locked-in customer commitments. The Indian-American CEO who co-founded SanDisk is running the only American company that makes the memory chips AI cannot function without.
articles.image_caption: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, the Kanpur-born co-founder of SanDisk
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, born in Kanpur and educated at BITS Pilani, runs the only US maker of the memory chips powering the AI boom. His company is also building a $2.75B plant in Gujarat — creating jobs and entry points for India's semiconductor ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A War 5,000 Miles Away Is Slowing India's Chip Dreams. Tata's Dholera Fab Is Hit Hardest.
articles.excerpt: The West Asia conflict has disrupted supplies of helium, bromine, and sulphur — exotic materials that India's greenfield semiconductor fabs need and cannot yet source independently.
articles.image_caption: A researcher handles a silicon wafer inside a semiconductor fabrication facility
articles.nri_angle: NRI semiconductor engineers eyeing return-to-India roles at Tata or Micron face a new variable: project timelines pushed back 6-12 months as supply chains India doesn't control buckle under geopolitical stress.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
